sel-k1-s-for-c.what: the sine's selection for k = 1 takes S for C. KNOWN FALSE, MEASURED: at x = 1/4 (3E800000) the planted graph gives 0 (00000000) and sin (2 pi x) is exactly 1 (3F800000). Refused where the proof decides the selection for k = 1

big-2p22.what: the switch to the constant results at 2^22 for 2^23 (half turns are still binary32 numbers there). KNOWN FALSE, MEASURED: at x = 4194304.5 (4A800001) the planted graph's cosine gives 1 (3F800000) and cos (2 pi x) is exactly -1 (BF800000). Refused at the end of the proof's branch of the whole numbers, which the planted graph does not take where the proof does

arg-pl-for-ph.what: the argument is multiplied by cos32's second constant PL for PH (the wrong one of the two imported). KNOWN FALSE, MEASURED: at x = 1/4 (3E800000) the planted graph's sine gives 248D3132 (about 6.1e-17) and sin (2 pi x) is exactly 1 (3F800000). Refused where the proof splits the argument's error into the rounding of v PH and the distance of PH from PI/2

q-2f.what: q = 2 f for 4 f (half turns for quarter turns). KNOWN FALSE, MEASURED: at x = 1/4 (3E800000) the planted graph's sine gives 3F3504F3 (about 0.7071) and sin (2 pi x) is exactly 1 (3F800000). Refused where the reduction needs q = 4 f

sel-k2-no-sign.what: the sine's last case (|k| = 2) without its change of sign. KNOWN FALSE, MEASURED: at x = 3F028F5C (about 0.51) the planted graph gives 3D809849 and sin (2 pi x) lies between BD809849 and BD809848. Refused where the proof decides the selection for k = -2

cn-2p52.what: the rounding constant is 2^52 for 1.5 * 2^52 (a negative v then leaves the window where binary64's grid is 1). KNOWN FALSE, MEASURED: at x = BE99999A (about -0.3) the planted graph's sine gives 3F737870 and sin (2 pi x) lies between BF737871 and BF737870. Refused where v + CN must lie in [2^52, 2^53)

cn-odd.what: the rounding constant one smaller, an odd number (ties then go to the odd whole number). NOT known false: MEASURED by the emitter stage (emit-measure-run2.txt) on the 633,224 lines of the frozen corpus, 0 results differ; a whole number within 1/2 is all the method needs. Refused only by the route of the proof, which moves the constant through round-to-nearest-even by a lemma that asks for an even whole number

hand-edited-graph.what: Graph.v with one blank added at the end of a line: the same graph for Coq, and not what emit_sincos32.py prints

prem-no-format.what: COSTURN32 for every real x, not only binary32 numbers. KNOWN FALSE, MEASURED: at the binary64 number 8388608.5 (not a binary32 number) the graph gives 1 and cos (2 pi x) is exactly -1. Refused where the proof takes the premise

concl-correct.what: SINTURN32 claims the correctly rounded result. KNOWN FALSE, MEASURED: at x = 3E80300C (about 0.25037) the graph gives 3F7FFFD3 and the correctly rounded sin (2 pi x) is 3F7FFFD4 (the first such input found going up from 3E800001, after 12,300; no sin line of the frozen corpus is misrounded). Refused where lemma F32 no longer fits

exact-quarter-zero.what: SINTURN32_EXACT says the sine of a whole number plus a quarter turn is exactly 0. KNOWN FALSE, MEASURED: at x = 1/4 (3E800000) the graph gives 1 (3F800000). Refused where the value 1 no longer fits

unit-half.what: SINCOS32_UNIT says the sine is at most 1/2 in magnitude. KNOWN FALSE, MEASURED: at x = 1/4 (3E800000) the graph gives 1 (3F800000). Refused where the bound 1 no longer fits

admitted.what: Reduce.near_bound (the nearest whole number of a v below 2^23 is below 2^23 + 2) ends with Admitted for its last step

b149-axiom.what: the fact 2^-149 = 2 * 2^-150, b149, is an Axiom of Core.v (the same text, its proof removed), used by the top theorem through arg_rel and core_abs

other-statement.what: Sincos32.v states, under the name SINCOS32_ALL, the proposition True and proves that

guard.what: sincos32_all from False, by a recursion whose termination check is switched off
